conviction_note: The stock is a $1.94bn cash box trading at about 86% of cash per share. Its print turns on one thing: whether a first acquisition is announced. EDGAR shows no 8-K under Item 1.01 or 2.01 through 2026-11-13, so no material deal had been signed or closed by about 2026-11-09. That leans slightly negative. Against it, the cash floor caps the downside and the lock-up passed on a +3.8% week, so p_up sits at 48. abs_move 3.5 is above the single prior reaction of 2.37%, because a first-deal announcement is a binary catalyst the one prior print did not carry. The findings sum to -0.6 and the scaled number is -0.14. Both are near zero and point the same way, so there is no real disagreement between them.
bar: Disputed and capped. Earnings Whispers (2026-11-08, https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/BXDC/23053) has $0.13 a share for Q3 against $0.08 in Q2, and does not say whether that is EPS or FFO. Stockanalysis (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/bxdc/forecast/, updated 2026-11-02) has FY2026 FFO of $41.17m ($0.46 a share) against H1 FFO of $7.1m. That implies about $17m (about $0.17 a share) a quarter in H2, so the two sources disagree. The company gives no guidance. My mechanical estimate is about $0.15 GAAP EPS / $0.155 AFFO: interest of $9.3m over the 46 days to 2026-06-30 (10-Q) gives about $18.6m for a full 92-day quarter, less about $2.8m of G&A and about $0.9m of commitment fees, with management fees waived, over 100.65m shares. The quarter's number does not move this stock; deployment does.
positioning_check: Short interest 5.53m shares, about 5.5% of shares outstanding, 2.39 days to cover, FINRA settlement 2026-10-30 (https://equibles.com/stocks/bxdc/shortinterest, via the sweep row). Not crowded. Options: unusable chain, no skew; put/call OI ratio 26.4 on only 766 contracts of total open interest, which is too small to read. Holders: Cohen & Steers fell from 16.69% (2026-05-31) to 13.65% (2026-09-30), per its 13G/A filed 2026-11-13. BlackRock reported a new 7.0% at 2026-09-30 (13G filed 2026-10-27). Blackstone holds 9.1%, bought at the $20 IPO price (13D, 2026-05-22). The 180-day IPO lock-up was reported to expire about 2026-11-10, and the stock rose 3.84% over the 5 days into the seal.

findings.finding: Six months after the IPO, BXDC has filed no 8-K under Item 1.01 (material agreement) or Item 2.01 (completed acquisition). The only 8-K since 2026-05-19 is the Q2 results 8-K of 2026-08-04, against a target asset size of $250m-1.5bn on about $2bn of assets, which would make any deal reportable. So no material data-center deal was signed or closed by about 2026-11-09, four business days before the seal. The Q3 release is likely to show the company still all-cash, measured against the 2026-08-04 call's claim of confidence in deploying IPO capital 'within three quarters' (that is, by about Q1 2027). The market's expectation is a first deal; Earnings Whispers counts 67% bearish sentiment.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is one prior print, 2026-08-04 (Q2, no deals, deployment 'within three quarters'): -2.37% (baseline). The stock then fell about 23% to the 52-week low by early November (Earnings Whispers), which is consistent with deployment patience running out.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock is down about 23% since the Q2 print and sits 6% above its 52-week low. If the market expected a deal it had not seen, BXDC would trade nearer cash per share (about $19.4) than $16.6. The unpriced part is the timing: a deal signed between 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-13 could still appear in the release, because its 8-K would not yet be due. The absence of a filing therefore lowers the odds of a deal in the release without ruling one out.
findings.independence: Quartr's Q2 summary of the 'within three quarters' target and the zero acquisitions at 2026-06-30 (https://quartr.com/events/blackstone-digital-infrastructure-trust-inc-bxdc-q2-2026_FTcvjs3f). The 10-Q says the company had neither purchased nor contracted to purchase any investment at 2026-06-30 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2100161/000210016126000007/bxdc-20260630.htm). I found no press release about a deal since 2026-08-03.

findings.finding: Q3 is the first full quarter of interest income on about $1.94bn of cash with management and incentive fees waived. Interest of $9.3m over the 46 days to 2026-06-30 scales to about $18.6m over 92 days, giving GAAP EPS of about $0.15 and AFFO of about $0.155 on 100.65m shares. That compares with $0.13 at Earnings Whispers and roughly $0.17 implied by Stockanalysis' FY FFO of $0.46.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 net income of $0.14 (AFFO $0.08), described by management as not indicative of future earnings, was followed by -2.37%. The interest-income line has never moved the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: A small mechanical beat against the $0.13 bar is likely, but the bar is disputed (FY FFO consensus implies about $0.17), and on a cash box the market looks through interest income. If this mattered, the stock would not trade at a 14% discount to the same cash.
findings.independence: Q2 press release (AFFO $7.69m over the 46 days, 99.2m adjusted shares): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2100161/000210016126000008/exhibit991-20260630.htm. It comes from the same issuer reporting period, so the two sources are not independent.

findings.finding: The manager's fee waiver ends on 2026-11-15, the day before the print. From then the base fee is 1.00% a year of market capitalisation, about $16.7m a year or about $4.2m (about $0.04 a share) a quarter at a $16.6 share price. That is about 25% of the all-cash earnings run-rate, and it starts while the capital is still undeployed. The release or call will show either the fee drag on the Q4 run-rate or a waiver extension.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None: this is the first quarter the waiver expiry is live.
findings.why_not_priced: The fee terms have been public since the 10-Q, so the drag is largely in the price. The unpriced part is whether the manager extends the waiver, with Blackstone's own 9.1% stake bought at $20. An extension would be a positive surprise; nothing announced so far points either way.
findings.independence: Quartr's Q2 summary confirms the waiver runs through 2026-11-15 (https://quartr.com/events/blackstone-digital-infrastructure-trust-inc-bxdc-q2-2026_FTcvjs3f). It rests on the same underlying 10-Q.

findings.finding: Cohen & Steers, the largest specialist REIT holder, cut its stake from 16,789,209 shares (16.69%, 2026-05-31) to 13,736,736 (13.65%, 2026-09-30), selling about 3.05m shares, or about 1.7 days of average volume. The 13G/A was filed on 2026-11-13. BlackRock separately reported a new 7.0% (7.06m shares) at 2026-09-30.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on prints. The selling took place within the 2026-08 to 2026-09 slide.
findings.why_not_priced: The amendment became public on the day of the seal. The selling itself is complete and already in the price, and a large index and active buyer offset it. It says the dedicated REIT investor lost some patience; it does not predict the print.
findings.independence: Original Cohen & Steers 13G (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1284812/000128481226000129/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X02/primary_doc.xml); BlackRock 13G (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2012383/000201238326003763/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X02/primary_doc.xml), which points the other way.

findings.finding: At $16.625, BXDC trades at about 86% of its cash. Cash was $1,943.4m at 2026-06-30, plus about $15m of Q3 earnings, over 100.65m shares, which is about $19.4 a share. A first acquisition, a waiver extension or any capital-return step in the release would narrow that 14% gap, and a no-deal print has the cash floor under it. That makes the reaction asymmetric upward relative to the deployment risk in the first finding.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; the discount widened from about 0% at IPO to about 14% now.
findings.why_not_priced: The discount is visible to anyone. What is not priced is a catalyst to close it, and the only one in the window is the release itself. This is an inference about the shape of the reaction, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The spot of 16.625 comes from the sealed baseline; Stockanalysis shows 11 analysts at Buy with an average target of $23.36 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/bxdc/forecast/).

findings.finding: On Blackstone's own Q3 call (2026-10-22), management said it had raised valuation cap rates, said yields on new data-center assets should rise as capital for AI infrastructure gets scarcer ('you'll be able to command a higher yield'), and cited tripled data-center leasing of about 6 GW. That supports the case that BXDC, as an all-cash buyer, can deploy at better entry yields, which is the line its call will be judged on.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy from the parent. The call did not mention BXDC, and the same call flagged market worry about the sustainability of AI investment and higher rates, which is part of why BXDC fell. Sized small as macro-to-company transmission.
findings.independence: Proxy only. The Q2 call's 'more opportunities than capital' comment points the same way (https://quartr.com/events/blackstone-digital-infrastructure-trust-inc-bxdc-q2-2026_FTcvjs3f).

findings.finding: In June 2026, a month after the BXDC IPO, Blackstone-affiliated funds sold a $3.5bn equity stake in three Northern Virginia hyperscale data centers to Digital Realty, at an expected stabilized cap rate above 6.5%, rather than to BXDC. The deal shows the affiliated pipeline does not automatically flow to BXDC, although these assets do not stabilize until 2027-28 and so did not fit the mandate.
findings.why_not_priced: Old and public. Its relevance is only that a question about related-party sourcing could come up on the call, so it is sized near zero.

findings.finding: Sell-side stance into the print: Citi moved to Buy on 2026-10-12 while cutting its target from $23 to $20; Bernstein kept Buy at $26 on 2026-11-02; the consensus of 11 analysts is Buy with an average target of $23.36, 40% above spot.
findings.why_not_priced: This is wire copy and fully priced; it is filed for the panel's context only.
findings.independence: Benzinga lists BMO cutting its target from $23 to $22 on 2026-08-05 (search snippet only).

baseline_tension: There is no skew and no usable chain. The +3.8% 5-day and +6.3% 20-day run-up off the 52-week low leans mildly up, against my slight negative lean on deployment. That is one reason p_up is 48 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (absence of a filing is not a cause): the no-8-K finding rests on a legal filing requirement rather than an unexplained drawdown, so it stays, but it is cut from -1.0 to -0.8 because it is inferred from an absence.
Rule 6 (bar disputed: $0.13 at Earnings Whispers against about $0.17 implied by the FY FFO consensus): the reported-quarter finding stays capped at +0.2.
Rule 5 (proxy): the Blackstone Digital Realty sale cut from -0.2 to -0.1; the Blackstone Q3 call proxy left at +0.2.
Rule 1 (a fact is not a reaction): the cash-discount finding cut from +0.4 to +0.3, because cheapness is not a catalyst.
Wire copy is priced: the analyst-stance finding cut from +0.1 to 0.0.
Rule 7: short interest checked (5.5%, 2.4 days to cover, not crowded) and there is no skew, so no change from positioning.
